result.title: HiGS: A Hierarchical Architecture for Fast Differentiable 3D Gaussian Splatting
result.summary: 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) makes one screen tile the cell of partitioning, the cell of rasterization, and the unit of parallel work. Partitioning favors large tiles and rasterization small ones, and with one unit per tile the densest tiles set the frame time. We present Hierarchically Tiled Gaussian Splatting (HiGS), a unified architecture for rendering and reconstruction that gives each role its own granularity: Gaussians are partitioned over coarse macro-tiles, rasterized over the fine render tiles within them, and processed in bounded depth-sorted batches. A dense region issues more batches instead of one longer unit, so frame time follows the work in a view rather than its densest tile. The same batches carry reconstruction: compositing supplies the transmittance and color needed to differentiate each one independently, leaving optimizer memory traffic as the dominant training cost. We fuse the optimizer into the backward pass, halve the parameters and moments it stores and updates directly, and defer appearance updates outside the view. HiGS renders scenes faster than every published method we evaluate, by the widest margin on views with uneven load, and reconstructs them faster and in less memory, at equal image quality and with exact front-to-back alpha compositing.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 HiGS，将 3D Gaussian Splatting 的分区、光栅化与重建批次解耦为不同粒度，并把优化器融进反向传播以降低训练显存与耗时。
AI.relevance_reason: 该文属图形渲染与重建的系统/性能工程，虽涉及可微渲染与调度，但优化对象是高斯参数与 tile 负载，与 VLM 的 latent 推理状态、证据使用或停止决策无实质联系，也未提供可迁移的具体机制线索。
